qs.q: Adrenocortical carcinoma is typically characterized by which clinical and pathological features?
o: A neoplasm arising from the adrenal medulla that exclusively secretes catecholamines
A small adrenal incidentaloma under two centimeters with a favorable prognosis
A large tumor often exceeding six centimeters with multi-hormone secretion
Benign clinical behavior that responds completely to local surgical resection
qs.e: Adrenocortical carcinomas are rare, aggressive neoplasms that are usually large at presentation and frequently secrete multiple hormones like cortisol and androgens. They carry a poor prognosis and are linked to specific cancer syndromes.

qs.q: A patient is evaluated for a newly discovered adrenal mass. Which molecular finding is most commonly associated with malignant adrenocortical carcinomas?
qs.e: CDC73/parafibromin is mutated in approximately 70% of adrenocortical carcinomas, whereas it is intact in benign adenomas. MEN1 and RET mutations are associated with MEN syndromes rather than primary adrenal carcinomas.

o: Benign clinical behavior that responds extremely well to surgical resection alone
Malignant tumor arising from the adrenal medulla that secretes excess catecholamines
Small encapsulated tumor under two centimeters with an excellent prognosis and hormonal activity
Large tumor often exceeding six centimeters, poor prognosis, and potential multiple hormone secretion
qs.e: ACC is rare but aggressive. Typically large at presentation. May hypersecrete cortisol, androgens, aldosterone, or estrogen causing mixed endocrine syndromes. Associated with Li-Fraumeni syndrome (TP53 mutations) and Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. 5-year survival ~35%.
